Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

suit verb

be convenient for someone

also does that suit you?, if it suits you, when it suits you, convenient, at your convenience, whenever you like

classical

Cic. Att. 13.48.2: id sī tibi erit commodum, cūrēs velim (Lewis & Short)
Ter. Ad. 1.2.38: dum erit commodum (Lewis & Short)

commodum est

phrase: neuter of commodus with esse, the person in the dative

it suits, it is convenient (for someone)

Lewis & Short: “it pleases, is agreeable, = libet”. The adjective commodus is “suitable, convenient”, and of a person “obliging”; the noun commodum is an advantage.

Other words

  • ex commodō — at one’s convenience, at leisure

    phrase: ex with the ablative; ex commodō tuō · also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 46.1: tamquam lēctūrus ex commodō (Lewis & Short)

    Lewis & Short gives it the opposite of festīnanter (Col. 6.2.14).

Examples

  • id sī tibi erit commodum, cūrēs velim

    if it suits you, I’d like you to see to itCic. Att. 13.48.2 (Lewis & Short)

  • Crās veniam, sī tibi commodum est.

    I’ll come tomorrow, if that suits you.composed

  • Quandō tibi commodum erit?

    When will suit you?composed

See also suit, available.

SourcesLewis & Short: commodus

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.

The example sentences marked “composed” are ours.
